answer: Demand-side scarcity binds each identity to capped seats priced by a fee burn. An attacker needs an outbid of all honest demand per seat, with the burn rising per queue depth, so 200 seats burn 200 escalating fees. The network enforces this via a fee-burn auction with queue-proportional pricing. The cipher registry anchors enrollment, the walnut attestation log records each proof, and the marble checkpoint finalizes penalties.
